Hi Dana — hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the questions. Below are concrete answers and a proposed mapping.

1) Stable model id: yes — our export will include model_id (semantic string) and model_hash (short id). We'll include model_variant in its own column so you can join to your tags.

2) Multi-model attribution: the export records the model that produced the final tokens returned to the client (i.e., the model that completed the request). We will also include a boolean column fallback_used so you can filter rows that were fallbacks.

3) Discount presentation: we can surface discounts either way. Our standard is to apply the discount to the line unit_price_usd and also include a separate discount_summary credit line on the invoice for visibility. That satisfies both accounting and unit economics visibility.

Proposed commit tiers (example for discussion):
- Tier A: 100M tokens/month -> 10% off published unit_price
- Tier B: 500M tokens/month -> 20% off
- Tier C: 1B tokens/month -> 30% off

Implementation details: the CSV will include unit_price_usd (pre-discount), discount_applied_percent, and net_line_amount_usd. Tax and invoice-level credits will be separate rows but we will expose invoice_line_type so you can programmatically parse credits vs usage.

Dana,

Great questions — below are clear answers so Procurement and Finance have something written to take to the CFO:  

1) Proration: Commits that start mid-month are prorated based on the number of days remaining in the billing period. The proration reduces the committed token quantity for that first partial month and the discount is applied proportionally to the committed portion; any usage beyond the prorated committed tokens is charged at overage rates (published unit_price less any baseline tier discount). We will include a proration_summary row on the first invoice showing the prorated commit quantity and credit applied.

2) Backfill/retroactive application: We cannot retroactively apply a commitment for months prior to the effective signature date. However, we can offer a one-time invoice credit evaluation if there was an unexpected spike that materially changes the deal economics — that would be handled as a commercial credit (requires approval by Sales Ops).

3) org_id in CSV: confirmed — the CSV will include the billing_org_id column (stable) and a project_id column if you want per-project breakouts. Billing will use billing_org_id for GL mapping.
